Overflow action "Palette   {key}" -> "Commands   {key}". _palette_hint untouched — it is still the action's reader and still takes its text from the bound QShortcut. tests/panel/test_bc_wave.py:209 amended by declaration with an R2-misc citation; three stale comments in that file that claimed the '/' telling rides the Commands tooltip were corrected in the same pass (the assertions themselves — a sum of '/' counts across placeholder + khint + tooltip — are site-agnostic and unchanged).

(2) ONE REGISTRY. Added command_palette.PANEL_ANSWERED_COMMANDS (frozenset of the five literals), a panel_answered field on PaletteEntry set at the one build path (build_palette_entries), and carried through tool_palette._load_entries via getattr(e, "panel_answered", False) so the AST-extraction test helper in tests/test_panel_finesse.py (which stubs command_palette with a SimpleNamespace) still works. _SLASH_COMMANDS stays as data with a comment saying so; L3b decides row by row. CommandPaletteWidget is untouched — no hidden widget deleted.

(3) RANKED SEARCH. New pure module-level command_palette.rank_row(query, title, desc, send) -> float (best of the three fields, built on the existing fuzzy_match: substring 1.0 / subsequence ratio / all-words 0.8, +0.2 prefix, +0.1 word boundary) and rank_rows(query, rows) (drops 0.0, sorts by (-score, arrival index) so ties keep today's order, returns a copy, empty query returns rows untouched). ToolPalette._refilter applies it AFTER the DO x WHERE chip filter, with the old substring filter kept as an ImportError fallback. One behaviour change I made deliberately: _populate takes grouped= and the context group heads are suppressed while a query is active — the heads describe the browsing sort (context, verb, title) and under a ranked list they would alternate row by row and say nothing.

HONEST LIMIT ON THE RANKING. fuzzy_match caps a substring hit at 1.0, so for the live query "/re" the row "/render" TIES at 1.0 with every "/recipes build ..." row, and the tie resolves to today's grouped order (a recipes row first). That is exactly what the mission specified ("ties keep today's order"), so I did not add a tightness tiebreak. The new test therefore uses explicit synthetic rows: the recipes row's send is the generated "Build this network recipe — ..." prompt (what _load_entries actually builds for a non-command category), which carries no "/" at all, so the render row genuinely outranks it; a third case pins that an "/apex recipes" row matching only as a SUBSEQUENCE survives at 0 < score < 1 and ranks second — something the old substring filter would have thrown away entirely. The live "/render" query is now measurably better: /render is the first row where it used to be alphabetical.

(4) THE OWNED AUDIT ROW, and the trap under it. The audit's check wants "/" IN inp.placeholderText(). The placeholder now reads "Ask SYNAPSE · / commands" and the Commands tooltip drops its "/" (-> "Browse commands · Ctrl+K"), so the composer still tells "/" exactly once (BC-4 unchanged). I measured candidates under hython offscreen at 340x760 first: the chosen copy advances 168px against a 182/184/185px viewport in curious/expert/ml, so test_composer_telling_reads_whole_at_340 stays green with headroom (the old failing copy was 245px).
